title: Open Problem: 5-Coloring complexity for H-free graphs with a P4 component
statement_text: The complexity of the $5$-Coloring Problem restricted to $H$-free graphs remains open when $H$ has exactly one connected component $C$ isomorphic to $P_4$, and $H - V(C)$ is an induced subgraph of $rP_3$ containing at least one edge for some $r \geq 1$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. $G+H$ is the disjoint union of $G$ and $H$, $rH$ is the disjoint union of $r$ copies of $H$, $P_t$ is the path on $t$ vertices, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. For fixed $k$, the List-$k$-Coloring Problem asks, given $G$ and lists $L(v)\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}$, whether $G$ has a proper colouring with each $v$ coloured from $L(v)$; the $k$-Coloring Problem is the special case $L(v)=\{1,\dots,k\}$. Both are NP-complete for $k\ge3$, and on $H$-free graphs they remain NP-complete if $H$ contains a cycle or a claw, so only disjoint unions of paths are of interest. Known results: 5-Coloring is NP-complete on $P_6$-free graphs (Huang) and on $(P_5+P_2)$-free graphs (Chudnovsky, Huang, Spirkl, Zhong). List-$k$-Coloring is polynomial on $(P_5+rP_1)$-free graphs for all $k,r$, and List-5-Coloring is NP-complete on $(P_4+P_2)$-free graphs. The authors prove that List-5-Coloring (hence 5-Coloring) is polynomial on $rP_3$-free graphs for every $r$, which gives a full dichotomy for List-5-Coloring: it is polynomial on $H$-free graphs iff $H$ is an induced subgraph of $rP_3$ or of $P_5+rP_1$. They also prove that $k$-Coloring is NP-complete on $2P_4$-free graphs (hence on $rP_4$-free graphs, $r\ge2$) for every $k\ge5$. Combining these results, the complexity of 5-Coloring (without lists) on $H$-free graphs remains open exactly in the stated case, where $H$ has exactly one component $C$ isomorphic to $P_4$ and $H-V(C)$ is an induced subgraph of $rP_3$ with at least one edge (for instance $H=P_4+P_2$ or $P_4+P_3$).
notes: Stated implicitly as a remaining open case after Theorem 7; no labelled environment.
paper_title: Complexity dichotomy for List-5-Coloring with a forbidden induced subgraph

title: Open Question: NP-hardness of List-k-Coloring on rP3-free graphs
statement_text: Does there exist $k \in \mathbb{N}$ for which the List-$k$-Coloring Problem restricted to $rP_3$-free graphs is NP-hard?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. $G+H$ is the disjoint union of $G$ and $H$, $rH$ is the disjoint union of $r$ copies of $H$, $P_t$ is the path on $t$ vertices, and $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$. For fixed $k$, the List-$k$-Coloring Problem asks, given $G$ and lists $L(v)\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}$, whether $G$ has a proper colouring with each $v$ coloured from $L(v)$; the $k$-Coloring Problem is the special case $L(v)=\{1,\dots,k\}$. Both are NP-complete for $k\ge3$, and on $H$-free graphs they remain NP-complete if $H$ contains a cycle or a claw, so only disjoint unions of paths are of interest. Known polynomial cases on $rP_3$-free graphs: 3-Coloring for every fixed $r$ (Broersma, Golovach, Paulusma, Song), and $k$-Coloring on $rP_2$-free graphs for all fixed $k,r$. The authors prove that List-5-Coloring restricted to $rP_3$-free graphs is polynomial for every $r$, which completes a dichotomy for List-5-Coloring on $H$-free graphs. Two of the three main ingredients of their proof (frugality of colourings and the handling of certain $P_3$'s) hold for List-$k$-Coloring on $rP_3$-free graphs for every $k$, but the third fails to extend to $k\ge6$, and they could not decide whether List-$k$-Coloring is NP-hard on $rP_3$-free graphs for some $k$. In contrast, they show that $k$-Coloring (even without lists) is NP-complete on $2P_4$-free graphs for all $k\ge5$.

paper_title: Complexity dichotomy for List-5-Coloring with a forbidden induced subgraph
